alt: Theme 2 has four topics: home, town, neighbourhood and region; social issues (charity and voluntary work, healthy and unhealthy living); global issues (the environment, poverty); and travel and tourism.
caption: Four topics; sub-topics are set under Social issues and Global issues only.

alt: Four linked steps for issue-based writing: name the problem (the issue is), link cause and effect (because of this, as a result, this leads to), propose a solution (a possible solution would be, if we ... would) and justify it (this would help because).
caption: Treat problem-and-solution phrases as core vocabulary for this theme.

alt: Two halves of one piece of writing. Describing a place uses the present tense, comparatives and past narrative; evaluating a problem uses impersonal constructions, cause-and-effect connectives and conditionals.
caption: Theme 2 mixes description and argument, so practise switching between them.

alt: In reading, sort each part of an issues text into describing a problem, proposing a solution or evaluating how well a solution worked. In travel writing, move from a past-tense recount of what you did to a present-tense evaluation of what you think now.
caption: Separate problem, solution and evaluation in reading; switch tenses in travel writing.

alt: A weak answer only says there is a lot of pollution. A strong answer names a specific local problem, gives its cause, proposes a conditional solution and closes with an opinion and a reason.
caption: Problem, cause, conditional solution, justified opinion: a reliable structure for this theme.
